candidates.title: The shared harness carries two hardcoded single-shape communicators while one binary carries the parameterized one that subsumes both, so the rank shape a test needs decides which of three types it reaches for

evidence.command: git grep -n -E '^ *(pub )?struct StubComm' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/tests/ ; git grep -l 'common::StubComm' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/tests/ | wc -l ; git grep -l 'Rank0Of2' 077dbe2c -- crates/cobre-sddp/tests/ ; git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/tests/simulation_pipeline_integration.rs | grep -nE 'mod common|struct StubComm|StubComm \{ rank'
evidence.output: tests/common/mod.rs:32 declares 'pub struct StubComm;' as a unit struct whose rank() returns 0 and size() returns 1; 20 integration binaries use common::StubComm. tests/common/mod.rs also declares 'pub struct Rank0Of2;', a second unit struct whose rank() returns 0 and size() returns 2, used by 4 files (common/mod.rs, mpi_wire.rs, node_native_backward_gate.rs, simulation_integration.rs). tests/simulation_pipeline_integration.rs:51 declares 'mod common;' and imports common::builders at line 52, then at line 78 declares its own 'struct StubComm { rank: usize, size: usize }' and instantiates it at 15 sites, 14 with size: 1 and one with size: 2 at line 1173. integration.rs:86 declares ShutdownComm and conformance.rs:40 declares LocalComm as two further local Communicator impls.
evidence.reading: The same concept is spelled three ways in one crate's test surface: a fixed 1-rank unit struct and a fixed 2-rank unit struct in the shared harness, plus a parameterized rank/size struct local to one binary that covers both shapes and shadows the shared name inside a file that imports the same common module. The collective bodies are not interchangeable as written, so this is fragmentation rather than a redundant copy: the local one panics via unreachable! on allgatherv, allreduce and broadcast, common::StubComm copies send into recv, and common::Rank0Of2 copies at the displs[0] offset. That difference is the reason a consolidation has to be deliberate rather than a delete, and it is also the reason a test author picks by rank shape instead of by semantics today.

candidates.fixShape: Replace the three shapes with one parameterized stub communicator in the shared harness that takes rank and size and carries an explicit mode for the collectives a given path must not touch, so the pipeline tests keep their assert-unused semantics as a stated mode rather than as a separate type. The two existing unit structs become constructor calls at their 20 and 4 call sites and the local copy in simulation_pipeline_integration.rs disappears along with the name shadowing. This is not a blind delete: the unreachable! bodies are load-bearing for the pipeline tests that assert no collective fires on the frozen path, and the displs-offset copy in the 2-rank shape must survive verbatim. Byte-neutrality: communicator behaviour on every currently exercised path stays identical, so no golden moves; verify against the tier-1 parity goldens, the rank-invariance permutation harness, and a single-rank versus two-rank MPI reproduction, which is the direct check for this candidate.

candidates.title: The sibling-versus-inline test homing split across simulation and production is not threshold-driven: one file declares both homes at once, four inline modules sit above the proposed threshold, and one sibling was extracted at eleven test fns

evidence.command: for every 5d manifest file: git show 077dbe2c:<path> | wc -l ; git show 077dbe2c:<path> | grep -n '^#\[cfg(test)\]' | head -1 ; git show 077dbe2c:<path> | grep -c '#\[test\]' ; plus git grep -n -E '^ *mod tests;|^ *#\[cfg\(test\)\]' 077dbe2c -- <the five sibling declaration sites> and git show 077dbe2c:crates/cobre-sddp/src/simulation/extraction.rs | sed -n '2156,2162p;2411,2413p'
evidence.output: Sibling form, 5 sites in the 5d manifest: lead_time/mod.rs:747-748 (mod 748, sibling 1493 L / 53 test fns), production/fpha_fitting/mod.rs:40-49 (sibling 2673 L / 89), production/hydro_models/production.rs:1097-1098 (sibling 2759 L / 66), simulation/extraction.rs:2412-2413 (sibling 7138 L / 87), simulation/pipeline.rs:1083-1084 (sibling 2827 L / 11). Inline form above the proposed threshold: production/energy_conversion/builder.rs first #[cfg(test)] at 246 of 1405 lines = 1159 test lines / 26 test fns; production/hydro_models/evaporation.rs at 398 of 1314 = 916 / 22; production/hydro_models/summary.rs at 114 of 804 = 690 / 6; simulation/types.rs at 593 of 1107 = 514 / 18. simulation/extraction.rs declares BOTH homes: '#[cfg(test)] mod transit_seed_tests {' at 2156-2157 with 4 test fns and its own private date and three_stage_dates helpers, then '#[cfg(test)] mod tests;' at 2412-2413 pointing at the 7138-line sibling. 32 of the 47 manifest files carry at least one #[cfg(test)]. The lint-scope hypothesis is falsified: builder.rs:247, evaporation.rs:399 and summary.rs:115 each open a multi-lint #[allow(...)] block on the inline module, and production/fpha_fitting/mod.rs:40-49 opens the same kind of block on the sibling declaration, so the #[allow] wrapper appears on both forms and does not explain the choice.
evidence.reading: This extends CD-007's class beyond the lp/builder directory it was measured in. None of the 14 inlineTestOutliers in the station inventory is a 5d file, and testing-architecture.md section 3.2 item 4 names only entries.rs, columns.rs, template.rs and layout.rs, so the simulation and production instances are unrecorded. Two facts are new rather than a re-measurement: a single file declaring two test homes simultaneously is not in CD-007's evidence at all, and the split here is provably not size-driven in either direction, since four inline modules exceed the section 5.1 proposal of roughly 500 test lines or 40 test fns while the smallest sibling was extracted at 11 test fns.

candidates.fixShape: Pick the single homing threshold that section 5.1 of the testing architecture proposes and apply it here as a lint rather than a judgment call. The immediately available and fully byte-neutral step is the two-homes file: fold the four transit-seed test fns and their two private date helpers into the existing sibling tests.rs that the same file already declares, so one file declares one home. The four inline modules above the threshold extract to sibling tests.rs files as the surrounding code is touched, carrying their #[allow] blocks with them exactly as the existing sibling declarations do. Byte-neutrality: moving a #[cfg(test)] module between an inline block and a sibling file changes no compiled non-test code and no fixture value, so no golden moves; the reproduction pair and the rank-invariance harness still run to confirm.

positives.subject: crates/cobre-sddp/src/test_support.rs as a live, consumed test-support surface
positives.why: The module is gated '#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]' at lib.rs:46-47 and 24 of the 40 integration binaries import it at the pin, so the mechanism section 5.2 of the testing architecture adopted on 2026-09-15 works as designed: crate-internal geometry, state-layout, k-fan and slot fixtures are shared from one place instead of being reconstructed per binary. Its 1 slow-tests attribute is the only such attribute in the whole 5d manifest.
positives.sanctionedBy: docs/design/testing-architecture.md section 5.2 and its Adoption (2026-09-15) note

positives.subject: crates/cobre-sddp/tests/common/builders.rs Spec-plus-Default-plus-make pattern
positives.why: StageSpec, HydroSpec, BusSpec and ThermalSpec each pair an exhaustive field list with a Default impl and a make_ constructor, so adding an entity field is one edit in this file instead of one per fixture. HydroPenalties carries no Default in cobre-core, which makes this the only place in the test surface where that field-add cost is O(1). It is the correct target for the consolidations proposed above, and the candidates ask to route more fixtures through it, never to fork it.
positives.sanctionedBy: docs/design/testing-architecture.md section 3.1 item 4 and section 5.1 Layer 1

positives.subject: Named inner-module consolidation already in use in the large exercising binaries
positives.why: anticipated_core.rs holds 10 named inner modules, anticipated_scenarios.rs 5, hydro_sim.rs 8 and filling_commissioning.rs 4, each grouping a fixture family inside one integration binary rather than spawning a binary per family. That is the domain-binary shape section 5.1 Layer 1 proposes, reached with plain inline modules instead of #[path] files, and it is why the link cost of this corner of the suite is 4 binaries rather than 27.
